node.label: Jacques Le Goff
node.date_label: “Temps de l’Église et temps du marchand” (1960) · La Civilisation de l’Occident médiéval (1964) · La Naissance du Purgatoire: French original (1981) · The Birth of Purgatory: Arthur Goldhammer translation (1984)
node.description: A medieval historian who connects representations, everyday conditions and social organization. Jean-Claude Schmitt’s account, reproduced in the EPHE institutional notice, describes his medieval synthesis as attentive to material vulnerability, gestures, towns and intellectual activity. His work on purgatory advances a historically specific account of an intermediate place in the afterlife; that chronology remains a thesis to assess. His essays on medieval temporalities also supplied an explicitly acknowledged resource for E. P. Thompson’s discussion of work discipline.
node.representative_figures_and_works: “Au Moyen Âge: temps de l’Église et temps du marchand” (1960); La Civilisation de l’Occident médiéval (1964); La Naissance du Purgatoire (1981); The Birth of Purgatory, translated by Arthur Goldhammer (1984).
node.scope_note: The monographs and Le Goff’s 1960/1963 essays are not newly read. Schmitt’s interpretation is attributed; Thompson’s p. 56 provides direct named-use testimony. The original Purgatory publisher/contents qualification remains. French originals and Goldhammer’s translation are distinct; no career interval or exclusive Annales identity.

proposed_edges.relationship: Relates medieval representations and everyday material conditions within a social history attentive to belief and vulnerability.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Substantive characterization is attributed to Jean-Claude Schmitt’s account reproduced in the EPHE notice. The existing Purgatory publisher record is supplementary; it does not establish that the monograph was read or that its chronology is uncontested.

proposed_edges.relationship: Supplies a specifically acknowledged resource on merchant and ecclesiastical temporalities in Thompson’s 1967 time-discipline essay.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Primary p. 56 and n. 2 checked afresh: Thompson explicitly identifies Le Goff’s contrast and cites the 1960 and 1963 essays. This records that limited use, not the whole derivation of Thompson’s argument or a universal account of modernization. Le Goff’s cited essays remain unread here.
